# UAV Companion

> An open-source, static web map of the areas where small drones may fly (or are restricted), starting with Hubei, China, with Singapore planned. It is a planning aid, not flight advice: the official platform for the place (for China, UOM) must be checked before every flight.

People use it to plan drone travel. If a person asks you to prepare waypoints from a travel itinerary, produce a GeoJSON file in the format below. The person pastes your reply into the app (Trips tab, "Plan with an AI"), sees a preview, and confirms. The app checks the flight zones itself, so do not state zones, permissions or legal advice.

## For AI assistants

- [Prompt and format](ai/prompt.md): the exact instructions and an example reply. Follow it. (Paths here are relative to this file.)
- [JSON Schema](ai/schema.json): machine-readable description of the format.
- [Example](ai/example.geojson): a valid reply.

Key rules, in short:
- Reply with one GeoJSON FeatureCollection in a single code block.
- Each Feature has properties.name (required) and optionally type (home, hotel, takeoff, landing, photo, train, airport, hazard, residence, other, food, attraction, shopping, nature, transport, meeting; "hotel" is shown as Accommodation, "transport" is not a train station or airport), note, date and endDate (YYYY-MM-DD with the year; endDate is the last date of a multi-day stay), day (itinerary day, 1 = first) and order (position within the day). date, endDate, day and order are all optional: omit them when unknown, and never guess a year.
- If the whole itinerary is one trip, add a top-level "trip" object ({name, country, startDate, endDate, description}; name is required, and so are the dates whenever the itinerary has them; the app asks the person for dates you leave out). Give a day number only when there are no dates: the app works the day out from the dates. The app creates the trip and puts every place in it except a residence.
- "home" is the drone's home point (where flights start and return to). "residence" is the traveller's own home, only if the itinerary asks for it. Do not confuse them.
- Coordinates are [longitude, latitude] (WGS84), and only when accurate for that exact place. Never estimate or invent them. If unsure, set geometry to null and give properties.query (venue, address, city, country, in English) and optionally properties.queryLocal (the same place in its local script, tried if English finds nothing); the app looks it up and marks the result unverified.

## About the data and privacy

- Markers, notes and settings stay in the visitor's browser and are never uploaded.
- Zone data is served as static files; there is no API to call and no account.
